comment: Legal, governance, workforce, organisational, and change-management considerations are described as sitting beyond the architecture’s structural description. This could reinforce an artificial separation between architecture and implementation, even though these factors constrain architectural choices.

anchor.note: p.47 l.Lines 121-125 read as the printed page; section 3.2 agrees

public.text: Legal, governance, workforce, organisational, and change-management considerations are described as sitting beyond the architecture’s structural description. This could reinforce an artificial separation between architecture and implementation, even though these factors constrain architectural choices.
public.suggestedRevision: Clarify that these considerations are not represented fully in the core structural views but remain architecture requirements and constraints that must be linked to relevant components, services, and implementation decisions.
